documentation: Alongside the Kritikhamba there were 7 other pillars of different sizes spread out throughout a gated enclosure. Measurements from the base: Pillar 1 - 30x109 / Pillar 2 - 28x131 / Pillar 3 - 22x73 / Pillar 4 - 30x119 / Pillar 5 - 29x65 / Pillar 6 - 26x67 / Pillar 7 - 27x124 / Kritikhamba - 50x266
description: The lineage of the kings of Yatse is drawn from the Dullu inscription. This stele (kīrtistambha) roughly 2.5 metres tall gives a dynastic list matching Tibetan chronicles. At the top is a Buddhist symbol and Om mani padme hum.
source: Samuel Grimes / Giuseppe Tucci / Surya Mani Adhikary

documentation: Michāgāũ Stupas / Stele — A total of 14 stupas spread out the complex. Stele measurements are 41x182x10.
description: 13 chörtens dating from 1482 to 1501 CE.

documentation: Series of scattered remains around the vihara with some at the museum.
description: Kakre Vihar - oldest temple in Surkhet, rediscovered in 20th century. Built possibly in 13th century by Ashoka Challa. 200+ pillar stones found along pilgrimage route from India to Surkhet.

documentation: Two pillars at Uttarganga. One tilting and venerated by locals. Second pillar split and rejoined with a rod. Horse capital at Jaleshwor temple.
description: Four pillar stones - markers of ancient route to the south.
Impressive pillar stone nearly 2m high with seven lines of text. Yogi Naraharinath deciphered date as Sake 1037.
Three pillar stones. First worn but upright. Second highly decorated with Lhasa image of soldier on horseback, circle, stupa, and 4.5 lines of script.
Inscriptions and archaeological specimens dating to 13th century. Colophon mentions Ripu Mall as ruler in 14th century. Numerous mounds with old bricks, terracotta images, sculpted lions.

documentation: Found pillar with faint inscriptions mentioning Ananda Malla. Shiva temple completed 30 years ago.
description: Fort site controls movements to/from Dullu/Dailekh and India. Strategically important. One line inscription mentions Ananda Malla - possibly 15th century AD.

documentation: Saw terracotta chaitya, lions as temple guardians, Buddha reliefs, Gandharan-looking head.
description: 4-sided pillar stone with symbolic representation of Buddha / Maitreya / Tara / Lokeshwor.

documentation: Rectangular enclosure with stupa-like top. Epigraph on lintel in good condition. Structure next to current road.
description: Water receptacle made by chief-minister Devavarmii in 1334. Prthvimalla mentioned as great religious king. Colossal cistern built with cyclopean stone blocks.
Ashok Challa issued inscriptions dated 1255 and 1278. Refers to himself as Khasha-Rajadhiraja (emperor of the Khashas).
Confirmation of deed of Krachalla on reverse of copper plate grant. Inscribed Sake era 1145 (1223 AD). Krachalla invaded and subjugated Kumaon in 1223.
Ashoka Challa conquered Garhwal as far as Uttarkashi, evidenced by inscription in Barahat Vishwanath temple.

documentation: Collection of shivalingas, god reliefs, Buddha relief in bhumisparsha mudra with Krachalla inscription. 4 warrior figures on stone pillars.
description: Stone pillar inscription from Asokachalla - first recorded use of Nepali language. One of 3 centers where Agni was worshipped due to eternal flame.
Land grant charter of Abhayamalla recording opponents shot dead by arrows.
Land grant charter under Prthvimalla - opponents shot dead by arrows.
Land grant issued by Prithvimalla from Dullu.
Malayavarma became ruler of Karnali after Abhayamalla. Inscription states he is Raja. Mentions queen Ratnamala.
Inscription by Yasovarma - Prithvimallas chief minister known as Mahamandalesvara.
Inscription by Devavarma on lintel of small reservoir bearing name of Prithivimalla. Lekhaka Istidasa also mentioned.
Inscription reading Sri Taradevischiram jayatu - reference to Taradevi, prominent woman in Khasa court.
Vinayak Panchadeval built by Aksayamalla. Shikhara style temple with inscription on lintel.
Nivasthana - one of 3 centers where Agni was worshipped due to eternal flame powered by underground natural gas.
Sirasthina - one of 3 centers where Agni was worshipped due to eternal flame.
Ripumalla copied Abhisamayalankara in 1313 from Surkhet. First use of Vikram Sambat dating. Shalu monastery of Tibet.
Inscription documenting king Ripumalla copied Laghuratnatraya inspired by meditation of Lokanatha.
Land grant (Birta) from Abhayamalla to a Brahmana.
Land grant (Birta) from Abhayamalla to a Brahmana.
Bilingual land grant (Tibetan/proto-Nepali) from 1321 AD documenting patron-saint relationship between Adityamalla and monastery lamas.
Land grant from 1328 AD documenting patron-saint relationship between Punyamalla and monastery lamas.
Stone inscription kept on wall of Mahankala temple near Kankrevihar. Left by Asa sahu and Rueradevi dated 1292.

documentation: Śrīḍhuskā Stūpa — Stone structure with square base. Stupa destroyed and remade about a year ago. Inscription still legible.
description: Stupa with om mani padme hum in Ranjana script. Square plan with stepped garbha.
Buddha figure in meditative posture with standing Tara on roadside pillar.
Figure of celestial nymph carved on stone block from Kankrevihar ruins. Flying posture with necklace, bangles, aksamala.
Three life-sized stone lion sculptures on roadside of royal palace area. Large eyes and open mouths.
Kaskrkot place now in ruins on ridge overlooking Pokhara valley. Domains of Khasa reached here.
Adityamallas son Pratapamalla left no heir so Punyamalla (Pala descendant who married Adityamallas daughter) became king.

documentation: Shiva temple made of stone with 16th century inscription written by Ram Krishna from Benares. Names of Pratap and Mana Shahi of Raskoti lineage inscribed.
description: Shiva temple with inscription dating to 16th century.

documentation: Remains of Dullu Palace - seat of the Bam(?) kings. Only foundation walls remain. Turning into dumping site.
Two devals side-by-side. Inside has become a trash dump. Small god figure on lintel of 2nd Deval.
description: Patingini Deval

documentation: Bijaya Bhagwati Mandir next to old palace. Contains epigraph claiming temple is ishta devta of Khasa Malla and Pala kings.
Pillar with normal design on capital. On way to Baleshwor. Measurement: 30cm x 170cm.
Flat pillar on other side of classical Khasa Pillar.
3 pillars of different sizes inside army camp - design consistent with Khasa Malla pillars. Access denied.
Two pillars - one has stupa similar to kirtikhamba. Has inscription. Taller: 37x101, shorter: 24x73. Local claims from 1323.
Building built during reign of Rajendra Bir Bikram Shah Dev. Newari style windows.
Opposite museum - small Hanuman temple with broken lion remains, possibly from Dullu Palace or Khasa Empire.
Inscription at right of temple in style of Kritikhamba. Seems to begin with om mani padme hum. 55x85.
Shiva Temple built in Kathmandu pagoda style during Shah era. Buddha sculpture behind being actively worshipped.
Lamji Panchadeval - set of 5 devals with one in middle surrounded by 4 others.
description: Govinda Acharya built these temples, contemporary of Jitārimala.

documentation: One pillar with stupa in middle and circular lotuses. Inscription in proto-Nepali barely legible. 42x90.
12 pillars (1 fallen) - most follow Khasa Malla typology. Various measurements recorded.
Satkhamba - 7 pillars in good condition. 4 pointed tops, 2 circular. Pillars 4 and 5 have visible inscriptions.
Two pillars in Khasa typology - capital has spear tip. Pillar 1: 30x224. Pillar 2: 30x220 with triangle base and 4-pointed knots.
4 pillars on hilltop. 3 display Khasa Malla typology, one smaller and bent.
Two pillars near main bazaar. Pillar 1 has person carved on back.
Two steles - taller resembles Kritikhamba. Pillar 1: 56x222x19, Pillar 2: 50x139x17. Positions changed 4 years ago.
5 devals in Raskoti layout. Large deval has bricks removed/amalaka on ground.
Fort from Rasikot kings era, later used by Gorkhalis. Canon from unification period.
Narayan Temple - two-storied Kathmandu style. Stone tablet inscription in Nepali. Temple: 33x66x8.
4 pillars - 3 normal Khasa typology with triangles/spirals. Shorter one has circular bulb top. Locals say rearranged.
Single deval in Khasa Malla style - bottom painted white. Fountain with two taps below.
5 pillars of different sizes. One sunk into ground. Wall built around them.
Modern fountain with 3 Khasa pillars. Two original, one center added later. Concrete poured over most.
Top-half broken, bottom remains. Middle of field with overgrowth. Similar architecture to other devals.
Typical Raskoti layout. Area turned into fields. Most devals half broken. Tree growing into them.
22 devals of all sizes. Clusters of 2, 7, and 9 devals. Two connected by pavilion.
Two taps, one functional. Flower motif. Water tank in front, possibly over older receptacle.
Commemorative pillar with warrior on horse with sword. Lotus motifs. Some blue paint by locals. 40x195x15.
Raskoti or Khasa plan. Sunk into ground with massive stones. Motifs on sides. Right spout broken, left fitted with pipe.
Most detailed deval seen. Typical Raskoti layout. Niches with indigenous gods. Animal/human motifs on pillars.
New temple with golden dome roof and wooden masts. Two stone inscriptions. Named for sage who drained Jumla lake.
Stele with faint devanagiri. Swastika on top register. 44x105x13.
Shiva Mandir - circular temple with two stone inscriptions. Left: 50x87x7, Right: 52x70x9.
Fountain with animal/human motifs and Kathmandu-style tap. 3 stupas, one with inscription.
Dry fountain in classic layout. One stupa remains - two destroyed for road expansion.
Single deval with fountain below. Structurally intact. Two deity figures with inscriptions below.
Two stupas side-by-side. Locals say fountain once existed here.
Fountain still has running water. Deval destroyed during road construction.
description: Goha (Guthichaur) was seat of Pala Kingdom. Stone temple documented by Tucci.
source: Surya Mani Adhikary / Tucci / Prayag Raj Sharma / DANAM

documentation: Two stupas - one with intact dome. Motifs similar to fountains. One has sanctum for Buddhist deity.
Pillar with flower motif. Top pattern like other pillars. Writing not legible. 37x122x9.
Shiva temple with modern materials. Interesting dome possibly imitating Chandannath.
8 Khas era pillars. Others destroyed/repurposed as fencing. Pillars 2 and 8 well preserved.
Bayalkāṭhiyā Pavilion on raised platform. All stone with hypostyle roof. Stele eroded with bullet holes. 55x185x8.
Fountain destroyed - locals took stones for homes. No trace remains.
Babira Masta Temple - modern tiered pagoda/Kathmandu style.
Babira Masta Temple (2) - smaller branch temple.
Stele with stupa in middle, circular motifs (chakras?). Writing not legible. 48x200x7.
Half deval remains with humanoid figure at entrance. Local legend about protective stones caused destruction.
Mani Malika Mandir - active masta temple with wooden carved struts and stone/clay sculptures.
Half stupa - destroyed during Maoist insurgency. Stele eroded. 45x103x8.
4 pillars - 2 standing, 2 fallen. Stupa and triangle motifs.
Stele with beaded outline and dharmachakra motif. 42x124x10.
Curved deval design - no front stones, no amalaka.
Museum dedicated to the Khasa.
Half broken stele with triangular/stupa motif.
3 devals of different sizes. Middle largest. Two with amalakas and stone slabs pointing to each other.
Dharmachakra motif on top, Devnagiri writing below. 40x165x10.
Defunct fountain in typical layout. New tap installed above.
Bairam Mandir - modern with wooden poles resembling Khasa stone pillars. Old temple remains present.
Jacha Dhārā - functional fountain. Lintel has 3 figures including Buddha. Stele inside may be 10th century Tibetan inscription.
description: Potentially oldest writing in Karnali, predating proto-Nepali at Padukasthan.

documentation: Two devals facing each other. Left larger, both partially buried.
Classical layout with two fountain heads. Motifs on side. Within metal fence.
Hindu Temple - modern, brick and white paint.
5 pillars of varying condition. Various stupa and triangle motifs.
Stele submerged in canal. Measurements not possible.
Top part of pillar. Sun/moon motifs, warrior on horse, triangular stupa.
Broken pillar on ground. 39x95x10.
Rasipatan Temple - small hut built where deval stood.
Two pillars. Taller: 32x145x11 with flower motif. Shorter: 31x95x10 with prominent stupa motif.
Temple with repurposed kritikhamba as door. Lions from Saubada site. Pillars with devanagiri.
description: Remains of Khasa Palace in main administrative capital Sinja.

documentation: Ruins of older structure - possibly deval. Amalaka converted to shivalinga. Locals say these are Khasa palace ruins.
Large stone blocks from Khasa palace. Well-preserved lion on platform. Three headless smaller lions.
Sera Stone Inscription of Ripu Malla. Tibetan om mani padme hum on top, devnagiri below. Still legible.
description: Documents Ripumalla copying Laghuratnatraya inspired by Lokanatha.

documentation: Kham Gaite Pillar - slanted with sun/moon motif and flower motif. 38x164x8.
Mahadev Mandir - wooden temple 10-15 years old. Only entrance door is old.
Two steles - tall 36x173x9, short 36x74x7. Sun/moon motifs. Location moved due to landslide.
Classical fountain with one intact tap. Small deval-like structure above. Yellow wooden humanoid figures.
3 steles. Sun/moon motifs, vishvavajra, beaded framing. Devnagari inscriptions barely legible.
Top half of deval visible, rest buried. Fountain buried by landslide.
Rugā Maṣṭā Temple - 20th century stone/wood/tin. Sun with face/mustache resembling old Nepali flag.
First stele in good condition with beaded framing, sun/moon/visvavajra. 5 more eroded steles on incline.
Kālikā Mālikā - new temple with old parts scattered. Pillar 30x107x15. White painted sculpture.
Old Kolikholā Pillar moved to secretarys house. Worshipped as Shiva. Bas relief stupa. 49x100x~8.
Top half of deval visible. Fountain buried by landslide.
Pillar broken in two. Beaded motif, sun/moon, triangle stupa. Locals took other pillars to houses.
Small tablet with inscription mentioning Bikram Samvat. Found while digging house foundation. 25x46x3.
